value.answer: For short-term use, it looks fairly safe for most adults. Low doses, around 5 mg or less, taken for a short while have been well tolerated in studies. The common side effects are mild, like headache and feeling drowsy, and they go away when you stop. Long-term safety is less clear. A preliminary study shown at a heart meeting linked a year or more of use to more heart failure, but it's not peer-reviewed and can't prove cause, and a later 2026 analysis found no link, so it's still open. It can also interact with blood thinners and antidepressants, so check with a doctor or pharmacist before taking it, especially if you're on other meds.
